repository.name: impostor
repository.root_summary: Impostor is a pnpm workspace for a mobile-first, in-person social deduction party game. The repository contains a React/Vite single-page web app, a Cloudflare Worker API with one Durable Object per room, and a shared TypeScript domain package for game rules, state transitions, scoring, words, and public/private snapshots.
repository.architecture_style: TypeScript monorepo with a browser SPA, same-origin Worker API, room-scoped Durable Object state authority, and shared domain logic.

entry_points.summary: Top-level pnpm scripts coordinate development, build, typecheck, lint, tests, e2e tests, and Cloudflare deployment across workspace packages.

dependencies.description: The React app imports domain constants and types for room limits, modes, categories, avatars, player colors, and snapshots.
The app calls createRoom, joinRoom, createRoomSocket, and sends typed realtime commands through the API client.
The app stores, restores, and clears room session tokens through the session module.
Browser fetch calls POST /api/rooms and POST /api/rooms/:code/join, then opens a WebSocket at /api/rooms/:code/socket.
Vite proxies /api to wrangler dev locally; production expects same-origin /api routing unless VITE_API_BASE_URL is set.
The Worker imports domain rule errors and room functions to create players, build snapshots, and classify validation errors.
The Worker maps room codes to Durable Object ids with env.ROOMS.idFromName and forwards create, join, and socket requests.
The Durable Object applies state transitions, scoring, timer resolution, and snapshot creation through domain functions.
The Durable Object creates room_state, saves JSON RoomState rows, loads rows, schedules alarms, and deletes idle records.
Room creation/join issue signed tokens; socket handling verifies tokens before accepting a WebSocket session.
The Worker uses shared helpers for JSON responses, CORS, empty preflight responses, and JSON request parsing.
Domain state validation and round start logic read word categories from the code-owned catalog.
Wrangler config declares the Worker entry, production API routes, allowed origins, and Durable Object binding.
The web deploy script publishes Vite dist to Cloudflare Pages, and _redirects provides the SPA fallback.
GitHub Actions runs root pnpm install, format, lint, typecheck, test, build, and dependency audit commands.

data_flows.name: Host Creates A Room
data_flows.summary: A host submits profile/config data from the React app. The Worker allocates a room code and player id, forwards to the Durable Object, persists a new room, sets a room-scoped HttpOnly session cookie, returns public/private snapshots, then the browser stores the room session and connects over WebSocket.

steps.action: Host fills create-room form on /play and submits profile plus partial RoomConfig.
POSTs JSON to /api/rooms.
Generates a room code and host player id, then forwards an internal /create request to env.ROOMS.get(id).fetch.
Creates host player and RoomState through domain functions, persists state, schedules cleanup/timer alarm, and signs a 24-hour token.
Stores room code and player id in sessionStorage and starts WebSocket connection with the room cookie.

risks: Room token is stored in a room-scoped HttpOnly cookie and used by the Worker during WebSocket upgrade.
Production TOKEN_SECRET must be configured or the Worker falls back to a local-development secret.

data_flows.name: Player Joins A Room
data_flows.summary: A joining player enters a room code and profile. The Worker forwards join data to the room Durable Object, which validates lobby capacity/nickname rules, persists the new player, broadcasts joins/snapshots, and sets a room-scoped HttpOnly session cookie.

steps.action: Join form uses an explicit room code, /play?room=CODE, or /play?join=1 setup path.
POSTs nickname/avatar/color to /api/rooms/:code/join.
Uppercases the room code, creates a player id, and forwards an internal /join request to the matching Durable Object.
Creates player, validates joinRoom domain rules, saves state, broadcasts player.joined and snapshots, and returns token plus snapshots.

risks: Join is intentionally accountless; room code and signed token are the only membership proof.
Nickname uniqueness is scoped to room state only.

data_flows.name: Realtime Gameplay Command Flow
data_flows.summary: The browser sends JSON client commands over WebSocket. The Durable Object applies the command through domain logic, persists state, emits phase/resolution/game events, and sends public/private snapshots.

steps.action: UI interactions send typed ClientCommand messages such as ready, start, config update, suspect, accuse, reset, cancel, and heartbeat.
webSocketMessage parses JSON, reads SocketSession attachment, and dispatches by command.type.
Domain functions validate and mutate room state for ready, start, config, suspicion, accusation, kick, cancel, reset, and timer rules.
The Durable Object saves the mutated RoomState JSON and schedules the next alarm.
Broadcasts phase.changed, round.resolved, game.finished, command.rejected, room.snapshot, and per-socket private.snapshot events.

risks: Client and Worker define similar protocol unions in separate files, creating drift risk.
Most Durable Object command paths appear covered indirectly by e2e/domain tests rather than Worker integration tests.

data_flows.name: Public And Private Snapshot Boundary
data_flows.summary: The domain package separates public room state from per-player private role/word data. The Durable Object sends public snapshots to everyone and private snapshots individually per socket.

steps.action: buildPublicSnapshot omits impostor id and secret word from active rounds.
buildPrivateSnapshot returns current player's role and visible word, and only reveals secretWord/impostorId after resolution.
broadcastSnapshots sends room.snapshot to all sockets and private.snapshot to each socket using its attached playerId.

risks: Privacy depends on all UI/server paths continuing to use domain snapshot builders instead of exposing raw RoomState.

data_flows.name: Timer Expiry And Idle Cleanup
data_flows.summary: The Durable Object schedules alarms for active round end times or idle cleanup. Alarms resolve expired rounds or delete state after the configured idle TTL.

steps.action: scheduleAlarm sets the alarm to currentRound.endsAt during active unresolved rounds.
resolveTimerExpiry validates timer state and scores the round as impostor got away.
alarm deletes room_state when now - lastActiveAt exceeds ROOM_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS.

risks: Timer and idle behavior depend on Cloudflare alarms and Durable Object storage semantics.
Local and production behavior should be verified with Wrangler for alarm edge cases.

data_flows.name: Build And Deploy Flow
data_flows.summary: The root scripts build all workspace packages. Deployment publishes the Worker with Wrangler and publishes the web app dist folder to Cloudflare Pages.

steps.action: Root build runs recursive package builds; root deploy deploys Worker first, then web.
Domain build emits dist and declarations from src.
Worker build typechecks and deploys with wrangler deploy.
Web build typechecks and runs vite build; deploy uploads dist to Cloudflare Pages.
Cloudflare routes /api/* to Worker and serves the SPA through Pages with fallback redirects.

risks: Deploy script is manual; CI verifies build quality but does not show deployment automation.
Worker and Pages must stay aligned on same-origin /api routing or VITE_API_BASE_URL.

key_entities.name: room_state
key_entities.description: SQLite table created with id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, state TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at INTEGER NOT NULL.

key_entities.name: RoomState
key_entities.description: JSON-serialized canonical room state containing code, config, phase, players, rounds, timestamps, and currentRoundId.

key_entities.name: PlayerProfile
key_entities.description: Room-scoped player profile with nickname, avatar, color, host flag, readiness, connected flag, score, and joinedAt.

key_entities.name: RoundState
key_entities.description: Round state with impostor id, secret word, starting speaker, timer, accusation, suspicions, and optional resolution.

relationships: One room_state row stores one RoomState JSON object.
RoomState has many PlayerProfile records in players.
RoomState has many RoundState records in rounds.
RoundState references PlayerProfile ids for impostor, starting speaker, accusations, suspicions, and score deltas.
data_stores.migration_strategy: Wrangler Durable Object migration tag v1 declares new_sqlite_classes [RoomDurableObject]. Table creation is performed lazily in RoomDurableObject.ensureSchema().
data_stores.retention: Short-lived room recovery; idle cleanup after ROOM_IDLE_TTL_SECONDS, default 86400 seconds.

secrets_risk_notes: TOKEN_SECRET is documented as a production secret and should be set through wrangler secret put; do not commit real values.
apps/worker/src/index.ts falls back to a local-development token secret if TOKEN_SECRET is absent, so production secret configuration is a critical deploy check.
The browser authenticates WebSocket upgrades with room-scoped HttpOnly cookies instead of exposing room tokens in query strings.

architecture_decisions.title: Use Cloudflare Durable Objects for realtime rooms
architecture_decisions.summary: Cloudflare Pages, Workers, and Durable Objects are chosen to keep room state authoritative, room-scoped, low-cost, and close to WebSockets without adding a separate database.

architecture_decisions.title: Keep game rules in a shared domain package
architecture_decisions.summary: Both web and Worker import @impostor/domain; architecture docs state UI or Worker code should not reimplement scoring.

architecture_decisions.title: Room-scoped profiles and no accounts for MVP
architecture_decisions.summary: The product scope and cost model explicitly exclude global accounts and paid authentication.

architecture_decisions.title: Keep curated word lists in code
architecture_decisions.summary: Word categories are stored in packages/domain/src/words.ts and docs state CMS should wait until non-developer editing is needed.

constraints.description: Repository pins Node.js 24.18.0 LTS and pnpm 11.11.0 via Corepack.
Production architecture depends on Cloudflare Workers, Pages, Durable Objects, Worker WebSockets, Durable Object alarms, and Durable Object SQLite.
Web app only, in-person play only, room-scoped profiles, no accounts, and no long-term player history.
Public snapshots must not expose other players' roles or private words; private snapshots are per socket.

risks.title: Production TOKEN_SECRET must be configured
risks.description: The Worker falls back to a hardcoded local-development secret when TOKEN_SECRET is absent. That is useful locally but dangerous if a production deploy omits the secret.
risks.recommendation: Add a deployment verification step or startup guard that fails production deploys without TOKEN_SECRET, and keep the runbook check explicit.

risks.title: WebSocket auth depends on room-scoped cookies
risks.description: The client creates /api/rooms/:code/socket URLs and the Worker authenticates the upgrade from the room-scoped HttpOnly cookie.
risks.recommendation: Keep the API and app same-origin or same-site, preserve exact CORS origins with credentials, and verify room cookies are set during create/join smoke tests.

risks.title: Realtime protocol types are duplicated between web and Worker
risks.description: ClientCommand and ServerEvent unions exist in both apps/web/src/lib/api.ts and apps/worker/src/protocol.ts. Drift could create runtime protocol bugs that TypeScript cannot catch across packages.
risks.recommendation: Move shared protocol request/response/event types into packages/domain or a small packages/protocol workspace package, then import them from both app and Worker.

risks.title: Main React app file is a large multi-responsibility module
risks.description: apps/web/src/app.tsx contains routing, landing content, game shell, forms, lobby, round, results, timers, theme, and WebSocket orchestration in one file, making focused changes harder for humans and AI agents.
risks.recommendation: Split by screen/flow after behavior stabilizes: routing/app shell, landing, setup forms, room header, lobby, round actions, results, and hooks for realtime/session/theme.

risks.title: Worker Durable Object behavior has limited direct tests
risks.description: Domain rules have focused Vitest coverage and web e2e tests cover major flows, but Worker tests visible in the repo focus on token signing. Direct tests for routing, Durable Object persistence, socket command handling, CORS, and alarm behavior are not evident.
risks.recommendation: Add Worker-level integration tests around create/join/socket dispatch and key command paths, ideally with the Cloudflare Workers test utilities or a Wrangler-compatible harness.

risks.title: No explicit production observability instrumentation is visible
risks.description: Docs intentionally defer paid observability/analytics, and no logging, metrics, tracing, or error reporting integration is visible in source.
risks.recommendation: Document the current minimal observability stance and add privacy-preserving Worker error/log guidance before production traffic grows.

risks.title: Core runtime is Cloudflare-specific
risks.description: Durable Objects and their SQLite storage are a strong fit for this MVP but tie the stateful realtime room model to Cloudflare.
risks.recommendation: Keep the domain package pure and document Durable Object assumptions around persistence, alarms, and WebSocket sessions.

test_coverage_indicators: Domain package has Vitest coverage for room state transitions and scoring.
Worker package has Vitest coverage for room token signing and verification.
Web app has Playwright e2e tests for landing/play routing, theme persistence, disabled future mode, overflow, legacy room query, create/join/start, accusation, and restart flows.
Web Vitest config currently passes with no tests in src.
typing_indicators: TypeScript strict mode is enabled in tsconfig.base.json.
Workspace packages map @impostor/domain to source during local development.
Domain package emits declarations in its build config.
linting_formatting_indicators: ESLint 10 flat config with TypeScript recommended rules.
React hooks and React refresh lint rules apply to apps/web.
Prettier config sets printWidth 100, double quotes, and no trailing commas.
CI runs format, lint, typecheck, test, build, and dependency audit checks.
observability_indicators: No explicit telemetry, tracing, structured logging, or error reporting integration was found.
Cost model says paid observability should be added only when Worker logs are insufficient.
security_indicators: Room tokens are HMAC-SHA256 signed with Web Crypto.
Room token expiration is set to 24 hours in Worker code.
CORS allowed origins are configurable and production origins are set in wrangler.jsonc.
Private player data is separated through buildPrivateSnapshot and sent per socket.
No accounts or long-term player history are in MVP scope.

start_here.task: Understand repo purpose and runtime shape

unknowns.description: No explicit production observability provider or structured logging strategy was found. Cloudflare dashboard/log usage may exist outside the repo.
The repo documents Cloudflare projects, domains, and routes, but this static analysis did not verify live Cloudflare resources.
Direct Worker/Durable Object integration tests for WebSocket command handling, CORS, persistence, and alarms were not found in the visible test files.
A deployment runbook exists, but automated production release or rollback workflows beyond manual Wrangler/Pages commands were not found.
